author_contract.rule: Taskbook authorship and scheduler dispatch approval are separate capabilities. A researcher may author and publish a coherent taskbook, but no authoring or policy-review action makes the task READY.

scheduler_gate.rule: No taskbook file mutation is authoritative for READY or DONE. These states exist only in scheduler V2 after the corresponding Driver review.

legacy_compatibility.historical_ready_taskbooks: may be explicitly imported into V2 bootstrap registry as migration records
legacy_compatibility.rule: Legacy taskbooks are not rewritten solely for V7. Redispatch after V2 activation uses the scheduler registry and current policy digest.

task_origin_contract.rule: A free-discovery output cannot lose candidate provenance. If a published task exists because of a free candidate, its audited candidate id/state remain mandatory.

obvious_stage_continuation_rule.pattern: STAGE integer >= 2 in task_id or title
obvious_stage_continuation_rule.reason: Stage numbering is explicit continuation semantics and may not be relabeled NEW_DIRECTION to bypass the successor gate.

task_lineage_contract.semantic_anti_evasion_rule: Even without Stage naming, if the parent result is a necessary research premise/motivation and the new task is the next unresolved layer of the same mother route, classify it CONTINUATION. Renaming does not reset lineage.
task_lineage_contract.rule: PASS or DONE on a parent task is not itself evidence for a successor. A CONTINUATION taskbook is publishable only when its successor gate names a genuine new information gap, falsifiable outcomes, a stop rule, and whether an independent/alternative exploration path was considered.

optional_metadata.identity_lane: compact human-readable lane such as R012, R005C, P017
optional_metadata.parent_task_id: required when task_lineage=CONTINUATION; otherwise normally null
optional_metadata.successor_gate: required when task_lineage=CONTINUATION; otherwise normally null

rules: A taskbook defines task-specific work, not a particular conversation instance and not a copy of repository operating policy.
New taskbooks declare task origin and task lineage. A free-candidate origin preserves audited candidate provenance; a continuation preserves parent/successor provenance.
CONTINUATION requires parent_task_id and a complete successor_gate; stage numbering or parent PASS is never a substitute for the gate.
The taskbook body inherits current repository policy through research_taskbook_policy.json; generic repository policy must not be restated in the body.
Taskbook authoring uses tools/research_taskbook.py new, followed by task-local editing and policy review. Policy review can make the taskbook PUBLISHED-ready but never scheduler READY.
Any allowed author role may publish after policy PASS. PUBLISH immediately registers the task in scheduler V2 as PUBLISHED/NEEDS_REVIEW.
A Driver DISPATCH review is a separate scheduler event. If the publisher is itself a Driver, that Driver cannot review its own publication into READY.
Researchers never transition their own task from PUBLISHED to READY or from RETURNED to DONE.
Taskbooks never bind a fixed runtime Researcher-ID. Scheduler CLAIM resolves execution identity independently.
A free-research axiom candidate enters taskbook authoring only after its required Phase-B audit/maturity state, and its candidate provenance remains visible.
recommended_flow: write only task-local content and complete any successor gate
emit and append scheduler PUBLISH event; task is now PUBLISHED / NEEDS_REVIEW
an eligible Driver independently emits REVIEW stage=DISPATCH verdict=ACCEPT; task is now READY
executor CLAIMs, works, and emits RETURN rather than DONE
an eligible Driver emits REVIEW stage=RETURN verdict=ACCEPT; task is now DONE
